text: [See CG 00 01 12 07, Sec. 1, Coverage A, ¶ 2.e.] [3:368 - 3:374] Reserved. b. [3:375] Coverage under separate “personal injury liability” coverage? There may be a better chance of coverage for certain wrongful termination claims under CGL “personal injury liability” provisions (see ¶ 3:297). (1) [3:376] Accidental “occurrence” not required: Unlike “bodily injury liability” coverage, there generally is no requirement for an accidental “occurrence” for personal injury liability coverage. (2) [3:377] Covered “offenses”: Personal injury liability coverage is limited, however, to certain specific “offenses” (see ¶ 3:298). The following are the “offenses” most likely to be encountered in wrongful discharge cases: — false arrest, detention, imprisonment or malicious prosecution; — defamation or violation of an individual's right of privacy. [See Loyola Marymount Univ. v. Hartford Acc. & Indem. Co. (1990) 219 CA3d 1217, 1222, 271 CR 528, 530; and American Guarantee & Liab. Ins. Co. v. Vista Med. Supply (ND CA 1988) 699 F.Supp.
